  FINISHED AGENDA & DRAFT MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Stephen Wood called the meeting to order at 4:22 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present: Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Noble, Russell, Scott, Wood

  Commissioners Absent: Hilliard, Romero-Duran

Also present: Paul Duncan, Homeless Services Bureau Manager, Jennifer Santana, Community
Program Specialist.

Roll call was taken by Jennifer Santana.
  • For the record members Romero-Duran, and Hilliard were absent and unexcused.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  26-55558  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Homeless Services Advisory
  Committee meeting of Wednesday, June 3, 2026.

  A motion was made by Member Bedy, seconded by Member Chotiswatdi, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Noble, Russell, Scott, Wood
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Hilliard, Romero-Duran

2.  26-55614  Recommendation to approve the Mayor’s Fund Subcommittee grant application
  submitted by Disabled Resources Center, Inc. for funding in the amount of $7,750.

  A motion was made by Member Bedy, seconded by Member Noble, to

  Yes:  6  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Noble, Russell, Scott, Wood
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Hilliard, Romero-Duran

  • Members of the committee discussed the grant application and expressed
  concerns regarding the budget line item for bus passes in the amount of
  $450. Member Scott requested clarification on this expense, noting that bus
  passes may be available at no cost through programs offered within the City
  of Long Beach.
  • The committee voted to approve the grant application in the amount of
  $7,300, contingent upon receiving clarification regarding the budgeted bus
  pass expense. If the clarification supports the requested cost, the committee
  approved funding the application in the full requested amount. Member Scott
  moved to approve the substitute motion, and Member Russell seconded the
  motion.

3.  26-55615  Recommendation to receive and file updates from the Mayor’s Fund and Policy
  Subcommittee and the Continuum of Care (CoC) Homeless Services Advisory
  Committee (HSAC) representative.

  A motion was made by Member Chotiswatdi, seconded by Member Russell, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Noble, Russell, Scott, Wood
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Hilliard, Romero-Duran

  • Mayor’s Fund Subcommittee
  o Health Department staff Jennifer Santana provided an update
  regarding the Mayor’s Fund Balance, there are no current MOU’s
  open.
  o Staff are reviewing 5 new grant applications that were received.
  • Policy Subcommittee
  o Member Sarah Bedy provided updates from the last policy
  subcommittee meeting including the discussion around the Pilot
  Hygiene project that would be funded through the Mayor’s Fund. The
  recommendation letter that will go to the Mayor and Council was
  drafted and we wil be discussed and approved in a later item.

  Page 2 of 7
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, AUGUST 5, 2026
  1301 W 12TH ST, LONG BEACH, CA 90813
  LONG BEACH MULTI-SERVICE CENTER, 4:00 PM

  • CoC Updates
  o Member Patricia Scott provided updates regarding the last two CoC
  Board meetings. The Board discussed the FY 2026 NOFO process
  and project reallocation. After careful consideration, the Board
  approved the City's recommendations, which will ultimately impact
  several currently funded programs. Member Scott also shared that the
  Board discussed the proposed expansion of the CoC Board through
  the addition of nine new board seats. Staff will begin the solicitation
  process for applicants interested in serving on the newly proposed
  CoC Board seats.

4.  26-55744  Recommendation to discuss strategies on increasing public awareness of and
  support for Homeless Services projects and services in the City of Long Beach.

  A motion was made by Chair Wood, seconded by Member Bedy, to approve
  recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Noble, Russell, Scott, Wood
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Hilliard, Romero-Duran

  • Member Bedy discussed the goal of increasing public support for homeless
  services initiatives. The committee emphasized the importance of increasing
  donations to the Mayor's Fund to help build community support for current
  and future homeless services projects. To support this effort, the
  subcommittee drafted a script for use at commission meetings, public
  hearings, community meetings, and other public events. HSAC members will
  use this script to provide consistent messaging when engaging with the
  community.
  • Members also shared additional ideas for increasing public engagement and
  raising awareness of the positive work the City is doing to support individuals
  experiencing homelessness. These ideas will be explored further as part of
  the committee's ongoing community outreach efforts. Members shared
  additional resources that can be used to support these efforts.

5.  26-55665  Recommendation to review and approve the recommendations regarding the
  fencing around the Billie Jean King Main Library for submission to the Mayor and
  City Council for consideration.

  A motion was made by Vice Chair Scott, seconded by Member Noble, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6 Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Noble, Russell, Scott, Wood

  Page 3 of 7
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES

  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Hilliard, Romero-Duran

  • Member Bedy provided an update regarding the recommendation letter
  submitted to the Mayor and City Council concerning the fencing project
  around the Billie Jean King Library. The recommendations are intended to
  promote a transparent, collaborative, and human-centered approach to
  addressing homelessness, with the goal of achieving the best possible
  outcomes for future projects.

6.  26-55626  Recommendation to approve a proposal for a $50,000 budget plan for the
  Mayor’s Fund pilot hygiene project to submit to the Mayor and City Council with
  funding provided through the Mayor’s Fund.

  A motion was made by Member Noble, seconded by Member Chotiswatdi, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Noble, Russell, Scott, Wood
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Hilliard, Romero-Duran

  • Member Bedy provided a recap of the goal to allocate $50,000 from the
  Mayor’s Fund toward the proposed project.
  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan provided additional details regarding the
  approval process and potential challenges associated with implementing a
  project of this scope. He noted that the project would require coordination
  and approval from multiple City departments.
  • Staff will forward the recommendation to the Mayor and City Council through
  a TFF memo for consideration. Once feedback is received, updates will be
  shared with the committee. Final approval of the project will be determined
  by the Mayor and City Council.

7.  26-55617  Recommendation to receive and file the 2026 Long Beach Point in Time Homeless
  Count Report from the Health Department.

  A motion was made by Member Bedy, seconded by Member Noble, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6 Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Noble, Russell, Scott, Wood
  No:  0 None

  Page 4 of 7
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, AUGUST 5, 2026
  1301 W 12TH ST, LONG BEACH, CA 90813
  LONG BEACH MULTI-SERVICE CENTER, 4:00 PM

  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 2 Hilliard, Romero-Duran

  • Health Department staff member Dalton Dorr provided an overview of the
  2026 Point-in-Time (PIT) Count, which was conducted on January 22, 2026.
  • Staff presented a percentage-based comparison of PIT Count data over
  time. The overall number of individuals experiencing homelessness in Long
  Beach increased this year. The unsheltered population remained relatively
  consistent, while the sheltered population increased compared to the
  previous year.
  • Health Department staff Dorr also provided an update on veteran
  homelessness, noting that it has decreased over the past several years. A
  collaboration between the VA in Long Beach and Orange County, which
  provides additional resources and support services, may have contributed to
  the reduction among this population.
  • Additional data was discussed regarding demographics, family disruptions
  and financial /unemplyment percentages.
  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan stated that the rates of homelessness in
  an area are largely impacted by affordability. Increasing cost of rentals
  specifically studios over the past years has significantly increased. A third of
  rental household in this country fall behind on rent at some point. In three
  months of the renter aid program being open we have recieved 4,600
  applications of low income households behind on rent.
  • Staff and members of the committee had additional conversation regarding
  the information presented and the unsheltered community.
  • A member of the public provided a comment regarding shelter bed rates and
  occupancy.

8.  26-55616  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Staff
  Operations and Updates Report from the Health Department.

  A motion was made by Member Noble, seconded by Member Chotiswatdi, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Noble, Russell, Scott, Wood
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Hilliard, Romero-Duran

  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan provided and overiew on staffing and funding,
  due to the FY 2026/2027 there will be funding sources that will have

  Page 5 of 7
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, AUGUST 5, 2026
  1301 W 12TH ST, LONG BEACH, CA 90813
  LONG BEACH MULTI-SERVICE CENTER, 4:00 PM

  reductions. The city is facing reductions in a number of different areas.
  • There is a proposal to reduce to one mobile access center, currently the
  team is operating with one mobile access center.
  • The Health Department is set to propose its budget at city council on the
  18th of this month.
  • The California State FY 2026/2027 budget was passed with $900M
  allocation for HHAP. Budget within the state is challenging but staff are
  waiting to see what will be presented over the next year.
  • The City submitted ERF Round 5 funding to focus on addressing Union
  Pacific Railroad. If awarded programming would start in 2027.
  • Older adult shallow subsidy program is now up and accepting applications.
  The age requirement is for members age 62 and older or 55 or older with a
  disability.
  • Staff provided an update on the Renter Aid Program, noting that a
  dashboard has been created to track program activity. The program has
  experienced high demand during the three months that applications have
  been open.
  • Staff provided an update on the HUD CoC NOFO, with the application
  deadline set for August 26, 2026. Staff noted that this has been a
  challenging process due to recent changes and reallocation requirements. A
  framework has been approved to evaluate projects subject to potential
  reallocation over the coming years.
  • Staff provided an update on the 702 W. Anaheim shelter project.
  Construction preparations are progressing, and the Request for Proposals
  (RFP) process has closed. A proposed construction company selection is
  anticipated to be presented to the City Council in the coming months for
  consideration.
  • Staff discussed current weather trends and preparations for the upcoming
  winter season. The group discussed potential impacts on community
  members, including individuals experiencing homelessness, and the
  importance of planning for anticipated weather-related needs and
  challenges.
  • Members requested additional information regarding programs that are
  scheduled to sunset. Staff provided further clarification and additional details
  regarding the affected programs.
  • Additional questions that the committee had were discussed.

PUBLIC COMMENT

  • No public comment.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

  • Member Noble provided upcoming fundraiser event details and encouraged members to
